title: Compact Inspector: Inline recommendations & fail-safe controls for batching + cache
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Problem: Product teams struggle to tune batching and prefix/KV caching settings because the Console UX today disperses recommendations across pages, requires context switching to experiment, and lacks immediate safety nets for aggressive cost-saving changes. They need a compact, single-pane inspector that surfaces: (1) workload-aware recommendations, (2) inline explainers about quality vs cost trade-offs, and (3) one-click fail-safe guardrails to prevent regressions in latency or accuracy.

Goals: Provide a low-friction experience to review and apply batching/cache changes from any model-route page or rollout view. Reduce experimentation time, lower accidental regressions, and make cost impact transparent at the token/req level.

Scope: Design a Compact Inspector component that can slide out from route and rollout details. Key sections: header summary (current config + projected cost delta), recommendation card(s) with confidence score and expected TPS/latency impact, quick-simulate toggle (sample request replay with different settings), guardrail toggles (auto-fallback on perf drop, soft limits for accuracy), and an audit preview showing recent related deploys and evals. Provide microcopy explainers for common terms (e.g., micro-batching, KV hit-rate) and links to deeper docs.

Prototype requirements: - Figma prototype with route->inspector interaction and quick-simulate flows - Accessible keyboard interactions and condensed mobile layout - Variant screens for: conservative recommendation, aggressive cost-saving, and manual advanced edit - States for: no-data, low-sample, conflict-with-locked-policy

Acceptance criteria: 1) Usability test with 6 engineers/PMs showing median time to apply recommended config < 4 minutes. 2) Simulate mode demonstrates token cost delta and latency estimate inline for sampled requests. 3) Guardrails can be toggled during rollout and recorded in audit logs. 4) Hand-off-ready spec for frontend & product with annotated tokens/metrics and Figma frames linked.

Risks and tradeoffs: - Over-surface recommendations may encourage unsafe aggressive quantization/batching; mitigate via conservative defaults and frictioned aggressive actions (two-step apply). - Sample simulations may be noisy for low-volume routes; must clearly label confidence and require larger sample or dry-run for low-confidence suggestions.

Next steps: finalize two visual directions (compact/stacked), prototype quick-simulate interactions, align with Eng on required telemetry and sim harness endpoints.
comments: 2025-02-14 Liam O'Connor: Initial draft and problem framing. Pulled examples from Console heatmaps and recent support tickets about unexpected latency spikes after manual batching tweaks.

2025-02-16 Ava Martinez: Added the quick-simulate requirement. Suggested inline confidence markers and a fallback toggle tied to rollout policies. Filed follow-up ENG question about available sample-replay endpoint.
2025-02-17 Rajesh Patel (PM): Requested cost delta be shown per 1k tokens and per-req to match billing UX. Also asked for per-route historical KV hit-rate sparkline in header.

2025-02-18 Design critique: - Keep the inspector header to a single line on narrow screens. - Prefer 'Apply with guardrail' CTA over 'Apply' for aggressive presets. - Provide an 'Explain recommendation' tooltip with short causal chain (why increase batch size helps here).

2025-02-19 Engineering sync (ENG-4188): Confirmed endpoints for sim replay exist but require a new sampling flag. Agreed on telemetry events: inspector_opened, recommendation_applied, sim_run, guardrail_toggled.
2025-02-20 Accessibility review note: Ensure color contrast for confidence badges and add aria-live region for sim results. Keyboard users should be able to run and accept simulations without mouse.
2025-02-21 Ava Martinez: Updated final frames in Figma and prepared handoff checklist. Assigned frontend owner in ENG for implementation planning.
decision_log: 2025-02-18: Use conservative defaults for first release; aggressive presets require explicit two-step confirmation.
2025-02-19: Tie guardrail toggles to rollout policies so they can be temporarily overridden by Site Reliability with audit trail.
2025-02-20: Simulate should run against a 1% traffic mirror for medium/high confidence, otherwise show 'low confidence' and require larger dry-run.
